rule: on the practice quiz, the smallest eps at which some setting keeps at least 90% of the accuracy (NDCG@5) and at least 90% of the newcomer share of the design without privacy; at that eps, the most accurate passing m and split
justification: epsilon = 2 with each member counting for at most m = 3 groups (25% of the budget on the group sizes, the rest on the pair counts). It is the strongest privacy at which the design keeps at least 90% of its accuracy and of its slots for new or small groups on the practice quiz (at any smaller epsilon no setting keeps both: the most accurate one keeps 87% of the accuracy and 98% of the newcomer slots). On the test it costs 0.033 NDCG@5 (6.2%; NDCG@5 0.495 against 0.528) and stays far above today's BOING (0.131) and above the design that uses no statistics about others (0.424). A small m works best: clipping to 3 groups leaves out 26% of the memberships but lets the noise be much smaller. In plain words: whatever the suggestions are, they were at most e^2 = 7.4 times more likely with any one member in the data than without them, for one release of the statistics.
opt_in_reading: Everyone counts (under the noise) serves the members who opt in much better when few do: at 25% opt-in and epsilon = 2, they get NDCG@5 0.489 when everyone counts and 0.283 when only opted-in members count (without privacy 0.524 and 0.475). The noise has the same size whoever counts, so with a quarter of the members it drowns counts that are four times smaller. Counting only opted-in members would give the others complete protection instead of epsilon = 2; counting everyone, they are still never profiled (their own list is the default one) and appear only inside noisy totals. Without privacy, counting a quarter of the members also makes most groups look small, so the newcomer quota goes to groups that only look small (newcomer share 4.5% against 20.3%).

reasons.floor_rule: on the practice quiz, the strongest floor t (each noisy pair count loses t times the pair noise scale, stopping at 0) that still keeps 90% of the accuracy and of the newcomer share of the design without privacy
reasons.advice: With privacy on, word a "shared members" reason as an estimate, and quote a count only when it is at least 3 noise scales (6 members at the chosen setting). That rule alone does not remove the invented links (on the test 26% of these reasons name two groups that share nobody, and 15% of those quoting 6 or more), because the recommender picks the largest noisy overlaps and so selects the noise's extremes. The counts it quotes are also low (clipping leaves out the groups beyond each member's m).
